name: Deep voice masculinity meta
lead: The deep voice masculinity meta is the belief, found in looksmaxxing and related culture, that a lower voice pitch signals masculinity and dominance and so contributes to perceived attractiveness or status. The sources reviewed contain no community text or studies on these perceptions, so this article covers only the underlying voice facts.

Typical fundamental frequencies for adult speech are about 90 to 155 Hz for males and 165 to 255 Hz for females.[1] Adult male vocal folds are longer and thicker than female folds, which usually produces a lower pitch, and a larger male vocal tract also lowers timbre.[2][3]

paras: Pitch is shaped mainly by vocal fold length, size and tension. Averages are given as about 125 Hz for adult males and 210 Hz for adult females.[3] Conditions that add mass to the folds, such as Reinke's edema, lower the fundamental frequency.[3]

Proponents hold that a deeper voice conveys dominance and masculine status. Encyclopedic sources reviewed note only that voice can reveal speaker age and sex and convey emotion, and do not address attractiveness or dominance research.[2]
No studies found in the sources reviewed on voice pitch and perceived dominance; research on this topic may exist in psychology literature.

card.summary: The belief that a deeper voice signals dominance and masculinity; voice physiology is documented, the social claims were not examined here.
card.note: Sources reviewed did not cover perception research.

quick.overview:
The meta holds that lower pitch equals more masculine, dominant presence.

Sources reviewed document sex differences in voice pitch but not its social effects.
quick.mechanism: Pitch is set by vocal fold length, mass and tension; male folds are longer and thicker, giving lower pitch on average.
quick.risks: Attempts to deepen the voice by straining or irritants carry vocal health risks; the strain itself is described as a cause of injury.
